caption:
is washing your face with hot water bad?

Hot water more than doubled how much water the skin lost.

Hot, lukewarm or cold: what do you use? One word below.

In a 2022 study, 50 healthy adults soaked one hand in hot water (about 41°C) and the other in cold water (about 11°C) for 10 minutes. Water loss through the skin, a sign the skin barrier is under strain, went up about a third in cold water and more than doubled in hot water. Only the hot side turned redder. All of these changes were statistically significant.

It measured hands, not faces, and a 10-minute soak is longer than a face wash. But the direction is clear: the hotter and longer the water, the harder it is on your skin barrier.

Try two weeks of lukewarm water and short washes, and see if the tight feeling eases.

Send this to the one whose showers could boil an egg.

General education only. If your skin stays red, burning or flaky, see a doctor in person.
